package_info.package_versions: Orion Platform versions released between March 2020 and June 2020 (exact versions not specified in the report)
package_info.why_malicious: The package was compromised during the build process to include a backdoor (SUNBURST/Solorigate) that enabled remote attacker control over customer environments. The malicious code was inserted into a core DLL, digitally signed, and distributed via official updates, resulting in widespread downstream compromise.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (DLL load during Orion service startup)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code checks for signs of a legitimate environment, waits a random interval to evade detection, then contacts a remote command-and-control (C2) server, receives attacker commands, and executes them, enabling remote access and control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code introduces a hidden backdoor that communicates with external servers and executes remote commands, which is not expected in legitimate IT management software.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal DLLs in Orion should not initiate outbound network connections to unknown domains or execute arbitrary remote commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools may contact update servers, but not arbitrary C2 infrastructure or execute attacker-supplied code.
key_indicators: Outbound network connections to attacker-controlled domains
Randomized execution timing to evade detection
Execution of remote commands received from C2
Presence of obfuscated or benign-looking code in a core DLL

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to SolarWinds build infrastructure and injects malicious code into the Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in official software builds.

attack_chain.action: Malicious DLL is digitally signed and distributed via official SolarWinds update channels.
attack_chain.leads_to: Customers download and install trojanized updates.

attack_chain.action: When Orion services start, the malicious DLL loads and executes the backdoor logic.
attack_chain.leads_to: Backdoor establishes contact with attacker C2 infrastructure.

attack_chain.action: Backdoor receives and executes attacker commands, enabling lateral movement, data exfiltration, or further compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full attacker control of victim environments.

behavioral_signatures: Core DLLs initiating outbound network connections to untrusted domains
Execution of remote commands received over HTTP/S
Digitally signed binaries with unexpected network or process behaviors
file_indicators: Unexpected changes in core DLLs between official releases
network_indicators: Connections to known SUNBURST/Solorigate C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com and subdomains)
Unusual HTTP/S traffic from Orion servers to external IPs/domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected outbound network connections from Orion servers, especially to known C2 domains. Compare hashes of core DLLs (e.g., Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll) against known-good versions. Analyze process behavior for randomized delays and execution of remote commands. Alert on digitally signed binaries exhibiting suspicious network or command execution activity.
